vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clawd-zero-trust
Version: 1.1.7

This skill bundle is designed for Zero Trust security hardening of OpenClaw deployments. All scripts and documentation consistently focus on restricting network egress, enforcing least privilege, hardening configuration, and auditing the system. Key security features include transactional UFW rule application with auto-rollback (`egress-filter.sh`), script integrity checks (`enforce_profile_gate`), explicit handling of potential lockouts (`perform_reset_or_die`), and careful curation of allowed network endpoints and plugins. The `egress-filter.sh` script notably includes a fix to replace `eval` with direct argument execution, demonstrating a commitment to secure coding practices. There is no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or deceptive prompt injection in any of the files; instead, the skill aims to prevent such activities.

llm.summary: The skill's files, instructions, and requested actions are internally consistent with a Zero Trust hardening tool for OpenClaw — it modifies firewall rules and OpenClaw config as expected and does not request unrelated credentials or download arbitrary code at install time.

dimensions.detail: The name/description promise Zero Trust hardening; the repository provides audit, harden, egress-filter, PLP, and release-gate scripts that implement exactly those responsibilities. Required system tools (dig, ufw, curl, python3, jq) are referenced in the scripts and documented; no unrelated third-party credentials or network sinks are requested. Minor metadata mismatch (SKILL.md shows v1.1.6 while registry lists 1.1.7) but that is not a functional mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs operators to run included shell scripts that read/write OpenClaw config (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json), create state under the skill directory, and change host-level firewall rules via ufw. Those actions are in-scope for a Zero Trust hardener, but they are high-impact: the scripts require sudo to change UFW and can modify global OpenClaw settings. The SKILL.md and scripts default to dry-run and include canary/rollback logic, which reduces risk, but an operator should review scripts and run dry-run/canary before applying on production.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote install or download is specified — this is instruction-plus-local-scripts only. All code is bundled in the skill; there are no external URLs, URL shorteners, or archive extraction steps in the install spec. That limits supply-chain risk from the skill’s install mechanism itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials in metadata. It legitimately reads/writes OpenClaw configuration and writes state/logs under the skill/workspace paths. It does not request unrelated secrets. Because it modifies global agent config (openclaw.json) and system firewall, the lack of declared privilege requirements is notable but proportional to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true. It can be invoked by the agent (default platform behavior), and its scripts perform privileged operations (sudo ufw, edits to agent config). Autonomous invocation plus the ability to alter firewall and agent config increases blast radius if run without human oversight — the scripts mitigate risk with dry-run, canary, hash gating, and rollback, but operators should ensure the agent cannot auto-run these scripts unless intended.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to do what it says: audit OpenClaw, harden config, and enforce an outbound allowlist via UFW. Before you run it on any production host: 1) Review the scripts (egress-filter.sh, harden.sh, plp-config.sh, audit.sh) yourself to confirm the PROVIDERS list and behavior match your environment. 2) Run only dry-run and --verify first; prefer --canary on a test instance to validate rollback/verification behavior. 3) Back up ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and any firewall config/state so you can recover quickly. 4) Ensure UFW is installed and active and that whoever runs the script has sudo privileges (the scripts call sudo ufw). 5) Because the skill can change host-level firewall and global agent settings, avoid enabling autonomous/unsupervised execution unless you trust the skill and the operator context; prefer manual invocation the first few times. 6) If you rely on endpoints beyond the allowlist (custom providers), inspect and justify adding them to PROVIDERS before applying. If you want further assurance, run the scripts in an isolated staging environment and examine logs/state (.state/* and workspace/logs) produced during dry-run/canary.
